newsitem.title: ITALY: Genoa airport outlines cargo plans.
newsitem.headline: Genoa airport outlines cargo plans.

text.p: Genoa airport intends to double the size of its cargo facility to 6,000 sq m from the present 3,000 sq m by the year 2000, the airport authority (Aeroporto di Genova Spa-AGS) said.

This will form part of the 1998-2020 infrastructure development plan, but given the limited space available, the airfreight area will then be switched -- after 2005 --to the airport's west side on a 27,000 sq m site including 12,000 sq m of warehousing, it added.
The authority is also looking at a dedicated air cargo rail link to the airport, it said.

Other features of the overall cargo development plans, include backing operational facilities for forwarder, consolidator and cargo agent facilities as well as "fast track" procedures for trucked air cargo.
It is also planning a duty free "airport-port" zone, agreements with other airports to encourage air cargo traffic and will review road feeder traffic tariff policies.

The authority said that infrastructure investments under its development plans will amount to 40.4 billion lire in in 1998-2001, followed by 85.4 billion lire in 2002-2009 and a further 177.4 billion lire in 2010-2020.
At present the authority is 60 percent controlled by the Genoa Port Authority, with 25 percent held by the city's chamber of commerce and 15 percent by Alitalia.
Industry sources said that the Rome airport authority -- Aeroporto di Roma Spa(ADR) -- is a possible candidate for the Alitalia stake. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
